summary: Democrats win both houses of the US Congress, the US strikes Iranian sites near Hormuz amid talks, Ukraine talks are set, and Israel's coalition contest begins.

topics.heading: Democrats win control of both houses of the US Congress
topics.summary: Democrats won the Senate and, by AP and CBS projections, the House in Tuesday's midterms, ending full Republican control of Washington. Several races are still being counted, and Trump says he will veto Democratic bills.[^1][^2][^3]

lead.title: Democrats win Congress: How they did it, and what it means

alsoReported.title: Democrats take control of the Senate after winning key midterm races
Democratic Party gains US House majority in 2026 midterm elections

article: Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections. AP called the Senate for Democrats late on election night, and AP and CBS News project that Democrats also win the House of Representatives, which Republicans have held for four years[^1][^2][^3]. Al Jazeera's count early Wednesday had Democrats at 53 of the 100 Senate seats and leading in three more; several races are still too close to call, and final results could take days[^1].

Many of the Senate gains came in states Republicans have long held. Al Jazeera counts seven Democratic flips, including Texas, Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina and Maine[^1]. In Texas, James Talarico beat Ken Paxton, the first Democratic statewide win there in 32 years, and in Maine, Troy Jackson defeated Senator Susan Collins[^1][^3]. In the House, Democrats flipped seats in Texas, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Iowa and elsewhere, but the final size of their majority is not yet known[^3][^25].

Why it matters: a US president needs Congress to pass laws and budgets, and the Senate confirms judges and senior officials. AP says Senate control will reshape Trump's final two years and likely limit his agenda, including hopes for a more conservative Supreme Court[^2]. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, set to become Speaker, lists reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring health-insurance tax credits, ending the Iran war and rolling back tariffs as priorities[^3]. Committee leaders plan subpoenas, legal orders to hand over documents or testify, from January[^3].

AP says voters were driven by high prices, the war in Iran and concerns about corruption[^2]. Trump congratulated the Democrats but has also said "I'll veto everything"[^4][^1]. House Speaker Mike Johnson says Republicans "will not be deterred by the outcome of one election"[^3].

What next: the new Congress is sworn in on January 3, 2027, so the current one serves until then[^25]. My read: the likeliest result is two years of divided government, with fewer new laws, more investigations, and harder fights over budgets, tariffs and the Iran war.
topics.differences: Counts differ while votes are tallied. Al Jazeera lists seven Senate flips including Maine; AP's list of seven includes New Hampshire instead, and CBS also reports Maine[^1][^2][^3]. AP says Democrats needed a net gain of 3 House seats; Al Jazeera says 5[^2][^25].

topics.heading: US strikes Iranian sites near Hormuz as Iran calls Washington's reply 'unconvincing'
topics.summary: US forces hit Iranian air-defence sites on Qeshm Island and nearby, which Trump called a "minor attack". Iran says the US answer to its plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is "unconvincing", but Qatar says both sides remain in talks.[^5][^6]

lead.title: Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan 'unconvincing'; Trump confirms strikes

alsoReported.title: US strikes Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, official says, leaving unclear what comes next
Oil prices fluctuate after US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island

article: US forces struck Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz early on Tuesday. A US official told AP the strikes were limited and aimed at Iranian forces firing surface-to-air missiles at US forces; Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm and Hengam islands and near Bandar Abbas[^6]. President Trump confirmed a "minor attack" on an anti-aircraft site on Qeshm and said it "wasn't war"[^5]. He had said there would be no strikes before the midterms; the last known US attacks were in early September[^6].

Diplomacy continues alongside the strikes. Iran had offered to reopen the strait over two days if the US met seven demands, including lifting sanctions and ending the US naval blockade of its ports[^5]. The US did reply, and Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called the answer "unconvincing"[^5]. Qatar, the main mediator, says both sides "remain committed" to negotiating, and a Qatari official told Reuters that mediators expected feedback within 36 hours[^5][^7]. Iran's foreign ministry says any deal must end the fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon[^7].

At sea, attacks go on. UKMTO, a British maritime security agency, says two projectiles hit a tanker's engine room off Oman, with no casualties, and it counted a record 30 attacks on ships in October[^5][^7]. India says one Indian sailor was killed when a dhow, a wooden cargo boat, was struck[^7]. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim several tankers hit mines and caught fire; those claims have not been confirmed[^5][^7].

Why it matters: oil prices move with every turn, and they reach fuel and food prices everywhere, including Ontario. Brent crude, the global benchmark, fell more than 7% on Monday on deal hopes, then rose to nearly $107 a barrel on Tuesday after the strikes before falling back[^8]. What next: US media, citing officials, report plans for wider strikes that could begin as early as Wednesday[^5]. Vice-President JD Vance says he and Trump "feel pretty good" about a negotiated settlement[^6]. My read: both a deal and a wider fight remain possible this week.
topics.differences: The timing of the strikes differs: CBS dates them to Nov 2, while AP and Al Jazeera say early Tuesday, Nov 3[^7][^6][^5]. Monday's Brent close is given as $105.03 by CBS and $104.77 by The National[^7][^8]. Iran's state broadcaster claims 11 tankers caught fire over nine days, which CBS says is unsupported[^7].

topics.heading: Kremlin confirms Abu Dhabi talks as Russia launches more mass air attacks on Ukraine
topics.summary: Russia says three-way talks with the US and Ukraine will be held in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11. Meanwhile Russian drones and missiles hit Ukraine's energy system on two nights running, and Zelenskyy proposes halting energy strikes first.[^9][^10][^11]

lead.title: Kremlin confirms trilateral Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week

alsoReported.title: Russia Attacks Ukraine With 310 Drones, Striking Energy Sites and Infrastructure
Russia launches massive overnight attack on Ukraine, killing 29; Zelenskyy urges US to step up support

article: The Kremlin confirmed on Tuesday that three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States will take place in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, on November 10 and 11[^9]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky will lead Russia's team[^9]. US envoy Steve Witkoff calls the meeting "working-level" and says it will cover post-war security agreements and de-escalation[^9][^11]. He says US negotiators will also meet France, Germany, the UK, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week[^11]. The last US-mediated talks were in February, before the war with Iran began[^9].

The fighting has not slowed. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles in one attack, mostly at energy sites, and that a hospital in Kharkiv was hit, injuring 73[^11]. ANI reports at least 29 dead, and says the toll from Sunday's strike on an aid centre in Komyshuvakha rose to 29 with people still under rubble[^11]. Overnight into Wednesday, Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 310 more drones, 272 of which were shot down or jammed; energy sites in western Ukraine were hit and most of the city of Kovel lost power[^10].

Zelenskyy linked the timing to US election day: "The Russians believe that America will not notice this signal"[^11]. In Berlin on Tuesday, he said a ceasefire could be agreed without a meeting of leaders and proposed stopping strikes on energy as a first step[^10]. Ukraine is asking allies to speed up deliveries of air defence and interceptor missiles[^10].

Why it matters: winter is close, and attacks on power plants decide whether millions of Ukrainians have heat and light. What next: my read is that Abu Dhabi is a technical meeting, not a peace conference. A useful sign would be something small and checkable, such as an energy truce, rather than a broad deal on borders.
topics.differences: ANI's report does not make clear whether 29 is the national toll from the latest attack or the Komyshuvakha toll alone; yesterday's brief gave at least 26 for Komyshuvakha, citing the regional governor[^11].

topics.heading: Israel certifies its election results as Herzog begins talks on who forms a government
topics.summary: Israel's election committee delivered the official results and found no evidence the vote was compromised. Parties now tell President Herzog whom they back; Netanyahu's opponents hold 67 seats but disagree on much.[^12][^13]

lead.title: Isaac Herzog receives Knesset election results, begins mandate negotiations

alsoReported.title: Opposition chiefs meet, agree to launch coalition talks, but path remains unclear
Israeli forces kill four in Gaza as fifth Palestinian dies of wounds

article: On Wednesday, Justice Noam Sohlberg, chair of Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave President Isaac Herzog the official results of the October 27 election, saying he found no evidence the vote's integrity had been compromised[^12]. Likud had claimed, without evidence, that Qatar funded Arab turnout, and had tried to delay certification; Sohlberg rejected that[^13]. The result: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has 53 of 120 seats, the Jewish opposition parties 48, and the Arab-led parties Ra'am and the Joint List a record 19[^12].

Now comes the step that decides who gets the first try at forming a government. Herzog meets each party, smallest first, on Wednesday and Thursday, and asks whom they recommend[^12][^14]. Religious Zionism and Shas say they will back Netanyahu, while Avigdor Liberman, Naftali Bennett and Yair Golan say they will back former army chief Gadi Eisenkot[^12]. United Torah Judaism is undecided and may recommend no one[^14]. Herzog must assign the mandate by November 11; the nominee then has 28 days, plus up to 14 more, to win a majority of 61[^14].

The arithmetic is not simple. With Liberman and both Arab parties, Eisenkot could reach 67 recommendations, but his possible allies range from Liberman's right-wing party to Arab-led parties[^12]. Liberman says a government without the Arab parties is possible but has not said how[^13]. Opposition leaders met on Tuesday, agreed to start coalition talks and plan to replace the Knesset speaker, which could open the way to a state inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attack[^13].

In Gaza, the truce is a year old but still deadly. Al Jazeera, citing medics, says Israeli strikes killed at least four people on Monday; the Israeli military says it struck Palestinian fighters[^15]. Gaza's Health Ministry counts about 1,600 people killed since the truce began in October 2025[^15][^16]. Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative, arrived in Israel seeking permission to bring in tents before winter[^15].

Why it matters: Israel's next government will shape the next phase in Gaza and its part in the Iran war. The possible outcomes include a broad unity government, a minority government, or another election[^12].
topics.differences: Likud says the opposition is building a government "reliant on supporters of terrorism"; opposition leaders say they want to replace "the October 7 government"[^13]. Gaza tolls since the truce differ slightly between reports a day apart: 1,593 (Al Jazeera) and 1,599 (Middle East Monitor), both citing the Health Ministry[^15][^16].

topics.heading: US helped Venezuela strike a Colombian rebel camp, US officials tell the New York Times
topics.summary: Four US officials say American intelligence and drones supported Venezuela's Oct 30 strike on an ELN guerrilla camp near the Colombian border. A rights group counts at least 23 dead, including some civilians; there is no official toll.[^17][^18]

lead.title: US Said to Help Venezuela Strike Rebel Camp

alsoReported.title: EE. UU. ayudó a Venezuela en un ataque letal contra el ELN, según funcionarios

article: Early on October 30, Venezuelan helicopters and drones attacked a camp of the ELN, a Colombian guerrilla group, in Venezuela's Apure state near the border with Colombia[^17]. On Tuesday, The New York Times reported that four US officials, speaking anonymously, said the strike used American intelligence and drones; it is not clear who flew the drones[^18]. The Pentagon referred questions to Venezuela, and Colombia denied any role[^18].

Some background: the ELN, or National Liberation Army, is a left-wing armed group with about 6,000 fighters that operates on both sides of the border[^18]. Venezuela has been led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez since Nicolás Maduro was removed in January[^17]. The US has also been striking boats it says carry drugs, and the Times counts 244 people killed in those strikes[^18].

The death toll is disputed. Fundaredes, a Venezuelan rights group, raised its count from 9 to at least 23 and says some of the dead were not fighters, including a woman of about 60[^17][^18]. Other counts range from 8 to 19, and no official toll exists[^17].

Why it matters: if confirmed, this shows the US working with Venezuela's new leadership against an armed group on land, a step beyond its strikes at sea. My read: questions about civilian deaths and about who oversees such operations are likely to grow, especially as a Democratic Congress gains more power to demand answers.
topics.differences: The US role rests on anonymous US officials quoted by the Times; the Pentagon has not confirmed it[^18]. Death counts range from 8 to at least 23 depending on the source, and some of the dead may have been civilians, according to Fundaredes[^17][^18].

topics.heading: Chip stocks rebound and AMD beats forecasts after a week of doubts about the AI boom
topics.summary: After a sharp sell-off in AI shares, chipmakers led a rebound on Tuesday, and AMD reported revenue up 45% on data-centre demand. A senior Chinese regulator warned that AI investment is "overly concentrated".[^19][^20][^23]

lead.title: Nasdaq Bounces as Chips Lead AI Revival: Stock Market Today

alsoReported.title: AMD beats expectations as agentic AI sparks its data center revenue growth engines
AI investment is becoming overly concentrated, Chinese official says

article: Shares in AI and chip companies have swung hard. On Friday, October 30, the Nasdaq Composite, a tech-heavy US stock index, fell 2.9%, its worst day in nearly five months, after a weak forecast sent Intel's shares down about 29% and an earnings miss by Alphabet weighed on the sector[^21]. On Tuesday, chips led a partial rebound: the Nasdaq rose 0.8%, Nvidia gained 2.3% and AMD 3.7%[^19].

After markets closed, AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45% from a year earlier, with its data-centre business nearly doubling to 64% of sales[^20]. It forecast about $17 billion for the next quarter, above analysts' expectations, and chief executive Lisa Su said Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, Oracle and Meta use its server racks[^20]. Not all the news was good: Apple warned that rising memory-chip costs will squeeze its profit margin[^22].

Behind the swings is one question: will the huge spending on data centres pay off? Reuters notes investor worry about AI building paid for with debt[^22]. In Hong Kong on Tuesday, Xiao Yuanqi, a vice head of China's financial regulator, said global AI investment is "overly concentrated" and crowds out traditional industries by raising their borrowing costs[^23].

Why it matters, in my read: the AI boom now holds up much of the stock market and a growing share of business investment, so a slowdown would reach savings, jobs and energy demand far beyond tech. Strong sales for chipmakers and doubts about profits for the companies buying the chips can both be true at the same time.
topics.differences: Outlets differ on Intel's Friday drop: about 28.6% (Zacks) or more than 30% (SiliconANGLE)[^21][^20]. They also differ on whether Apple or Nvidia was the most valuable company this week[^19][^22].

topics.heading: Study says warming halted a Baffin Island ice cap that had grown for 2,000 years
topics.summary: Researchers dating plants at the edge of Nunavut's Barnes Ice Cap say it had been regrowing for about 2,000 years until warming since the 1960s reversed it. The report does not name the journal.[^24]

lead.title: Human-driven climate change may have halted the onset of a new ice age, according to new study

article: A team led by Nicolás Young and Joerg Schaefer of Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory studied the Barnes Ice Cap, about 6,000 square kilometres of ice on Baffin Island in Nunavut and a last remnant of the vast Laurentide ice sheet that once covered much of Canada[^24]. Using carbon-14 dating of plants exposed at the ice's edge, they say the ice cap began growing again about 2,000 years ago and kept growing until about 1960[^24].

Warming since the 1960s cut that regrowth short, the researchers say, which is why the report frames the finding as human-driven warming possibly halting the slow start of a new ice age[^24]. Canada's summer temperatures have risen about 2.1°C, and the North is warming about three times as fast as the global average[^24].

Why it matters: it suggests human influence on climate now works on geological time scales, not only on this year's weather. A caution: the Euronews report does not name the journal or say whether the study has been peer-reviewed, and it rests on one ice cap, so my read is that this is an interesting result to watch, not a settled conclusion[^24].

question.text: Democrats will soon control Congress while Trump keeps the presidency. Beyond which bills pass or fail, what knock-on effects could this split have on the Iran talks, on Canada's trade talks, or on how other countries deal with Washington?

read.title: Democrats retake House majority after 4 years
read.summary: A clear account of what a Democratic House can actually do from January, from subpoenas and investigations to the priorities its leaders have named, and what it cannot.
